content.text:
Found it. `src/rules.js` defines `DIRECTION` for `groceries/transport/utilities/dining` but not for `refund`, even though `refund` is a `KNOWN_CATEGORIES` entry. `signedAmount` falls back to `DIRECTION[category] || 1`, so refunds silently get treated as spend (+) instead of money coming back (-).

Verifying the math: with refunds negative, net = 138.50 (groceries) + 68.60 (transport) + 128.20 (utilities) + 64.25 (dining) − 218.65 (refund) = **180.90**, matching the bank exactly. With refunds wrongly positive it's 618.20 — exactly what `npm run report` prints today.

Fix: set `refund: -1` in `DIRECTION`, and make the fallback fail loudly instead of silently defaulting, so a future category added to `KNOWN_CATEGORIES` without a `DIRECTION` entry throws instead of quietly miscounting.

content.text:
`npm run report` now prints Net 180.90, matching the bank statement, and `npm test` passes 6/6.

## Root cause
`src/rules.js` listed `refund` in `KNOWN_CATEGORIES` but never gave it an entry in `DIRECTION`. `signedAmount` fell back to `DIRECTION[category] || 1`, so refunds (which should subtract from spend) were silently added instead — inflating Net from 180.90 to 618.20.

## Fix
- Added `refund: -1` to `DIRECTION` (`src/rules.js:15`).
- Replaced the silent `|| 1` fallback with a startup check: every entry in `KNOWN_CATEGORIES` must have an explicit `DIRECTION` mapping or the module throws immediately. This is the "can't come back quietly" part — if anyone adds a new category to `KNOWN_CATEGORIES` without deciding its sign, the app fails loudly at load time instead of miscounting.
- Added four tests: refund direction is `-1`, a refund reduces `net` in a small sample, every known category has a direction mapping, and the shipped `data/transactions.csv` reconciles to `180.90` end-to-end (this last one is the regression guard tied directly to the bank-mismatch symptom).
